 Judgment
This petition is filed by the petitioner against respondents for seeking compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by him in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

02. The brief facts of case of the petitioner is that:
On 14-10-2019 at about 03.45 a.m, the petitioner was travelling as a pillion rider along with his friend who was riding the Motor Cycle bearing No. (SCCH-3) 3 M.V.C.No.7711/2019 KA-02-KA-3732 came from Nelamangala to Bengaluru Highway Road and while they proceed at Peenya Flyover and at that time the rider of Motor Cycle had tried to ride with high speed, in rash and negligent manner and could not control over the Motor Cycle and dashed to flyover divider and caused the accident.
Due to this the petitioner sustained grievous injuries and immediately after the accident he was shifted to Sparsha hospital, Yeshwanthapura, Bengaluru, wherein after first aid treatment, he was referred to People Tree hospital, Goraguntepalya,
Bengaluru, wherein admitted as inpatient and has undergone surgery and discharged on 19.10.2019 and has spent huge amount towards medical treatment, conveyance,
nourishment etc., and prior to accident he was hale and healthy and was aged about 25 years and was employed with M/s Actio.in, Bengaluru as Movement Executive and earning income of Rs.16,554/- p.m.

Due to accidental injuries, the petitioner cound not able to do any work and could not earn any amount and thereby sustained loss of his entire earning till now and injuries caused permanent disability.

The accident occurred due to rash and negligent riding of the aforesaid offending Motor Cycle by its rider and in this regard the Peenya Traffic Police have registered a case (SCCH-3)
4 M.V.C.No.7711/2019 against the said offending Motor Cycle rider.

Hence, the respondent No.1 being the RC Owner and the respondent No.2 being the insurer of the said offending Motor Cycle, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- with interest and costs.
03. On service of notice, the respondent No.2 has appeared before the tribunal through its counsel and filed written statement.
Inspite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 did not appeared and hence, she was placed exparte.

04. The respondent No.2 in its written statement has denied the entire case of the petitioner and further denied the alleged accident, negligence of the rider of offending Motor Cycle, age, income,
occupation of the petitioner and nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and treatment taken by the petitioner and expenses incurred by the petitioner and contended that the rider of the Prathap .S vs Chikkathayamma on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91436056/
2 Motor Cycle was not holding valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident, the owner of the Motor Cycle has contravened the provisions of M.V. Act and Rules and they committed the breach of terms and conditions of the policy and admits that this respondent has issued policy of insurance in favour of respondent No.1 in (SCCH-3) 5 M.V.C.No.7711/2019 respect of Motor Cycle bearing Engine No.PFYWKB30329 and chassis No.MD2837AY3KWB 13127 pertains to Motor Cycle bearing No. KA-02-KA-3732 and the liability of this respondent if any, is limited to terms and conditions of the policy and subject to valid and effective driving licence of the driver in question.
The Motor Cycle in question did not involved in the accident nor caused accidental injuries to the petitioner and the petitioner was riding Motor Cycle in question at the time of accident, while riding Motor Cycle had skid and fall from Motor Cycle and sustained injuries and it is a case of self-accident.

The compensation claimed is highly excessive, exaggerated and hence, pray for dismiss the petition with costs against respondent No.2.
05.

On the basis of the above pleadings of the parties, my learned predecessor has framed the following Issues:-
ISSUES 01.

Whether the petitioner proves that he has sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 14.10.2019 at about 03.45 a.m. on NH-04,Tumakuru-Peenya Flyover Road, near Peenya Police Station Junction, Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent act of the riding the Motor Cycle bearing registration (SCCH-3) 6 M.V.C.No.7711/2019 No.KA-02-KA-3732 by its rider as alleged in the petition?
02. Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation?
If so, to what amount and from whom?
03 . What Order or Award?

06. The petitioner in order to prove his case, he himself examined as PW.1 and got examined the doctor who examined the petitioner and assessed disability as PW.2 and through them got marked 15 documents as Ex.P.1 to 15 and closed the petitioner side evidence.
On behalf of the respondent No.2, its Manager Legal and Doctor got examined as R.W.1 and 2 and through them got marked 3 documents as Ex.R.1 to 3 and closed its side evidence.
07. The learned counsels for the petitioner and respondent No.2 have argued on main matter and perused the records.

08. My findings on the above Issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1 In the Affirmative  Issue No.2 Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No.3

As per final order  for the following:-
 (SCCH-3) 7 M.V.C.No.7711/2019 Prathap .S vs Chikkathayamma on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91436056/
3  REASONS 09. Issue No.1:-
The petitioner in order to prove his case, he himself examined as PW.1 and in his chief-examination evidence he has reiterated the petition averments therein.

During the course of cross- examination by the respondent No.2 counsel he denied to the suggestion that on the date of accident he was riding the Motor Cycle and some other vehicle has caused accident to him and also denied to the suggestion that he gave information at Sparsha hospital that when he was riding the Motor Cycle some other vehicle came and he sustained injuries and denied to the suggestion that in order to get compensation eventhough he was riding the Motor Cycle belongs to his mother, he has falsely stated that he was proceeding as pillion rider in his Motor Cycle and also denied to the suggestion that the accident occurred due to his negligent riding and admits that the Police came to the hospital to take complaint and not to enquired him about the incident.

10. Further, PW.2 is a Doctor, who examined the petitioner and assessed the disability of the petitioner, has stated that the petitioner sustained open fracture dislocation of subtalar joint with fracture (SCCH-3) 8 M.V.C.No.7711/2019 of the medial malleolus and fracture of the right leg both bones with vascular injury type IIIC and he assessed total physical disability of the right lower limb at 42% and whole body disability at 14% and he has produced Case sheet, Clinical notes and X-ray as per Ex.P.13 to 15 and he also stated that the petitioner needs another surgery for removal of the implant and the estimated cost is around Rs.60,000/-.

During the course of cross-examination by the respondent No.2 counsel he stated that as of now petitioner is not under treatment and admits that fractures are united and implants are in-situ and the fracture positions are accepted.

Petitioner can walk independently without any aid and admits that after fractures are united petitioner can use limbs and admits that he has assessed physical disability and not functional disability.
11. Apart from the oral evidence, the petitioner has got marked 15 documents as Ex.P.1 to 15 on his behalf.
Ex.P.1 is copy of FIR filed by the Peenya Traffic Police against the rider of the offending Motor Cycle for his rash and negligent riding and caused the accident.

Ex.P.2 is copy of Complaint lodged against rider of the offending Motor Cycle which shows that the injured himself given statement at People Tree hospital (SCCH-3) 9 M.V.C.No.7711/2019 regarding the accident after two days of accident.
Ex.P.3 is copy of Spot Mahazar.
Ex.P.4 is copy of IMC report.
Ex.P.5 is copy of Sketch.
Ex.P.6 is copy of Wound certificate which shows the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident.

Ex.P.7 is copy of Charge Sheet which discloses that the Investigation Officer after thorough investigation has submitted Charge sheet against rider of offending Motor Cycle for his rash and negligent riding and causing accident and causing grievous injuries to the petitioner.

Ex.P.8 and 9 are the Discharge summaries of People Tree hospital,
Bengaluru, which discloses that the petitioner was admitted as inpatient in the said hospital twice for 11 days due to accidental injuries.
Ex.P.13 is Case sheet.
Ex.P.14 is Clinical notes and Ex.P.15 is X-ray.

12. On behalf of the respondent No.2 Insurance Company, its Manager Legal is examined as RW.1 and in his chief-examination evidence he has stated that petitioner himself was riding the Motor Prathap .S vs Chikkathayamma on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91436056/
4 Cycle and he skid and fall from the Motor Cycle and sustained injuries and it is a self accident and MLC of Sparsh hospital stated that petitioner sustained injuries while riding Motor Cycle and entries made in MLC are prior to the complaint being lodged and said petitioner is not (SCCH-3) 10 M.V.C.No.7711/2019 having valid driving licence and thereby, respondent No.1 breached the terms and conditions of the policy by handing over the Motor Cycle to the person who has not holding valid and effective driving licence.
13.

During the course of cross-examination by the petitioner counsel the RW.1 admits that offending Motor Cycle had insurance policy with the respondent No.2 and same is valid as on the date of accident and said policy is package policy and it covers pillion rider also and they have conducted internal investigation pertaining to the accident and they have not produced said report before the tribunal.

14. Further, the Orthopedic Surgeon at People Tree hospital as examined as RW.2 has stated that the history of accident was written as per information furnished by the relatives of the injured and Police intimation is sent to jurisdictional Police.
However, during the course of cross-examination by the petitioner counsel the RW.2 admits that he has not author of the Ex.R.3 MLC extract.
Said document was written by duty doctor Sajith and he do not know who given history of accident to the doctor and admits that condition of the patient was not mentioned in the said document.
Apart from the oral evidence, the respondent No.2 has got marked 3 documents.

Ex. R.1 copy of Policy with terms and conditions,
which indicates that said policy is package policy and it covers pillion rider also and as on the date of accident the policy is valid and is in force.

Ex.R.2 is copy of MLC extract of People Tree hospital wherein it is mentioned patient was pillion rider and Ex.R.3 is copy of MLC extract of Sparsha hospital, wherein it is mentioned alleged history of RTA while riding two- wheeler was hit by another vehicle.
But as admitted by the RW.2 doctor who wrote the said MLC is not summoned and examined.
Moverover, in the said document the vehicle number is not mentioned and it is mentioned that one Manjunath was accompanied with the patient.
But there may be chances of said Manjunath has furnished information regarding the accident.
Therefore, without examining author of said MLC, it is not clear that the petitioner himself riding the Motor Cycle and skid and fall and sustained injuries and it is self accident.
As per Ex.P.1 FIR, Ex.P.2 Complaint and Ex.P.13 Charge sheet, it indicates that the petitioner was pillion rider as on the date of accident and one Manjunath was riding the Motor Cycle.

Therefore, the petitioner has clearly (SCCH-3) 12 M.V.C.No.7711/2019 established and proved that the he has sustained grievous injuries in the accident occurred on 14-10- 2019 at about 03.45 a.m, at Peenya Flyover, on Nelamangala - Bengaluru Highway Road, due to rash and negligent act of riding of Motor Cycle bearing No.KA-02-KA-3732 by its rider, as alleged in the petition.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the affirmative.
16. Issue No.2:- This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the grievous injuries sustained by the petitioner in Road traffic accident.

Prathap .S vs Chikkathayamma on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91436056/
5 17.

The petitioner in his evidence and pleadings has stated that prior to accident he was hale and healthy and was aged about 25 years and was employed with M/s Actio.in, Bengaluru as Movement Executive and earning income of Rs.16,554/- p.m and has spent huge amount towards medical treatment, conveyance, nourishment etc., and prior to accident he was hale and healthy.
Due to accidental injuries, he become permanent disabled, loss of income and suffered pain and sufferings.

18. It is duty of the petitioner to prove his age, avocation and income, but the petitioner has not produced birth certificate, school records or SSLC (SCCH-3) 13 M.V.C.No.7711/2019 marks card to show his exact date of birth.
However, he has produced Ex.P.12 Aadhaar card.
Even though the said Aadhaar card is not authenticated document for the proof of age of any person, but in the absence of any other evidence, the same can be relied upon,
According to which, date of birth of the petitioner is mentioned as 23.10.1994.
The alleged accident occurred on 14.10.2019.
Therefore, it appears that at the time of accident the age of petitioner is 25 years.
Accordingly, this tribunal has assessed the age of the petitioner as 25 years as on the date of accident.

As per the ratio laid down by the Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and Ors. V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and Others case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 15 to 25 years is 18.
19.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and Ors. V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: With regard to his avocation and income, the petitioner has not placed any materials before the tribunal.
Therefore, in the absence of evidence regarding his avocation and income, this tribunal has to go by the Lok-Adalath Chart.
According to which the Notional income in relation to the accident of the year 2019 to be taken as Rs.14,000/- p.m.
Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the monthly income of the Petitioner is at Rs.14,000/-.

According to the evidence of PW.2, the Doctor who examined the petitioner and assessed the disability has stated in his chief examination that the petitioner has sustained sustained open fracture dislocation of subtalar joint with fracture of the medial malleolus and fracture of the right leg both bones with vascular injury type IIIC and he assessed total physical disability of the right lower limb at 42% and whole body disability at 14%.
However, considering the evidence of PW.2 and nature of injuries sustained and medical records, this tribunal has assessed functional disability of the petitioner at 10%.

Therefore, the loss of future income works out as under:
Rs.14,000/- x 12 x 18 x 10% = Rs.3,02,400/-.
21.

Attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges:- The petitioner has produced Ex.P.8 and 9 Discharge summaries, according to which the petitioner was admitted twice in People Tree hospital as inpatient totally for 11 days.
During the aforesaid period the petitioner might have spent a considerable amount towards attendant charge, special diet, transportation and nutrition.

Therefore, considering the duration of treatment, (SCCH-3) 15 M.V.C.No.7711/2019 towards attendant charges, extra nutritious food and conveyance charges, the Petitioner is entitled for Rs.30,000/- under this head.

Prathap .S vs Chikkathayamma on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91436056/
6 22.
Pain and sufferings:-

As per Ex.P.6 Wound certificate and as per evidence of PW.2 doctor,
Ex.P.13 Case sheet.
Ex . P.14
Clinical notes and Ex.P.15 X-ray, which indicates that on account of accidental injuries, the petitioner would have undergone pain and agony due to grievous injuries sustained.
Accordingly with regard to grievous injuries suffered in the accident, he is entitled for Rs.30,000/- under this head.
23. Loss of income during laid up period:-

As already discussed above, the petitioner has not produced any documents regarding avocation and income and this tribunal has assessed the notional income at Rs.14,000/- p.m and he has admitted in the hospital for 11 days as inpatient.
Hence, by considering the nature of injuries, treatment taken, duration of his stay in hospital, it is quite natural that petitioner could not have carried out his avocation for atleast 2 months.

Thus,
taking into account the notional income of the Petitioner, this tribunal award a sum of Rs.28,000/-
(Rs.14,000 x 2) under this head.
Medical expenses:-
As per Ex.P.10 Medical bills, the petitioner has incurred medical expenses of Rs.2,97,106/-.
Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.2,97,106/- under the head of medical expenses.

25. Loss of future amenities and unhappiness:- Since the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and disability assessed by the doctor and on account of the discomfort and unhappiness, the claimant has to undergo in his future life, it is just and proper to award a sum of Rs.30,000/-
towards future loss of amenities and unhappiness.
26. Future medical expenses:-
According to PW.2 doctor, the petitioner needs another surgery for removal of the implant and the estimated cost is around Rs.60,000/-.
But he has not produced any estimation with regard to future medical expenses.
However, by considering the facts and circumstances of the case, he is entitled for compensation of Rs.30,000/- under this head.
27. Therefore, the petitioner is entitled for compensation as detailed below:-
(SCCH-3) 17 M.V.C.No.7711/2019 Sl. Head of Compensation Amount No. in Rs.
1. Loss of future income 3,02,400-00
2 . Pain and Sufferings 30,000-00
3 . Attendant charges, extra 30,000-00  nutritious food and  conveyance charges

4. Medical Expenses 2,97,106-00  5. Loss of future amenities and 30,000-00  unhappiness  6. Loss of income during laid up 28,000-00  period  7. Future medical expenses 30,000-00 Prathap .S vs Chikkathayamma on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91436056/
7  Total 7,47,506-00 28.

Accordingly I hold that, the petitioner is entitled for total compensation of Rs.7,47,506/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a (excluding future medical expenses of Rs.30,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.

29. Regarding liability:- As per the evidence of RW.1, he admits that the insurance policy of the offending Motor Cycle is valid as on the date of accident and said policy is package policy and it covers pillion rider also and as per Ex.R.1 policy schedule, it also shows the insurance policy is valid and is in force (SCCH-3) 18 M.V.C.No.7711/2019 as on the date of accident.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the R.C Owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending Motor Cycle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

However, since policy of offending vehicle was valid and is in force as on the date of accident, the respondent No.2 being the insurer of offending vehicle shall deposit compensation amount of Rs.7,47,506/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a (excluding future medical expenses of Rs.30,000/-) from the date of filing of the petition till its realization.
30.
Further, the counsel for the respondent No.2 has relied upon the citation reported in MFA No.2006/2010 (MV) c/w MFA No.1763/2010 (MV) in a case of S.T.Deepu V/s The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.,.

entities.text: S.T.Deepu V/s The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: I have gone through the citation relied upon by the counsel for the respondent No.2.

But said citation is not amply applicable to the facts and circumstances of the present case on hand, as there is one month delay in lodging Complaint and FIR, but in the case on hand there is no inordinate delay in lodging the complaint.

In the instant case as the petitioner himself admitted in the hospital,
his complaint was taken by the Police in the hospital itself.
Therefore, the said (SCCH-3) 19 M.V.C.No.7711/2019 citation is not amply applicable to the present case.
Hence, distinguished.
Accordingly, I answered Issue No.2 partly in affirmative.
31. Issue No.3:

In view of reasons assigned to Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:-
ORDER
The petition filed by the petitioner U/Sec.166 of the M.V. Act, 1989 is partly allowed with cost.

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.7,47,506/- (Rupees Seven lakhs forty seven thousand five hundred and six only) (with interest at the rate of 6% p.a (excluding future medical expenses of Rs.30,000/-) from the date of petition till its realization.

The respondent No.2 shall deposit above said compensation amount with interest within two months from the date of this Judgment.
Prathap .S vs Chikkathayamma on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/91436056/
8

The petitioner is entitled to get release 70% of the award amount through E-payment directly to the petitioner account by obtaining the bank account details and remaining 30% shall be kept in fixed deposit in any scheduled bank for a period of three years, in his name.
The Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.

Therefore, it appears that at the time of accident the age of petitioner is 25 years.
Accordingly, this tribunal has assessed the age of the petitioner as 25 years as on the date of accident.
As per the ratio laid down by the Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and Ors. V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and Others case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 15 to 25 years is 18.
19.
With regard to his avocation and income, the petitioner has not placed any materials before the tribunal.
25. Loss of future amenities and unhappiness:- Since the petitioner has sustained grievous injuries and disability assessed by the doctor and on account of the discomfort and unhappiness, the claimant has to undergo in his future life, it is just and proper to award a sum of Rs.30,000/-
towards future loss of amenities and unhappiness.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the R.C Owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending Motor Cycle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
However, since policy of offending vehicle was valid and is in force as on the date of accident, the respondent No.2 being the insurer of offending vehicle shall deposit compensation amount of Rs.7,47,506/- with interest at the rate of 6% p.a (excluding future medical expenses of Rs.30,000/-) from the date of filing of the petition till its realization.
30.
Further, the counsel for the respondent No.2 has relied upon the citation reported in MFA No.2006/2010 (MV) c/w MFA No.1763/2010 (MV) in a case of S.T.Deepu V/s The New India Assurance Co. Ltd.,.
But said citation is not amply applicable to the facts and circumstances of the present case on hand, as there is one month delay in lodging Complaint and FIR, but in the case on hand there is no inordinate delay in lodging the complaint.
In the instant case as the petitioner himself admitted in the hospital,
his complaint was taken by the Police in the hospital itself.
